title: Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program Status Rules: Holds, Resumption and Administrative Closure
content:
An active Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program is placed on hold for exactly one recorded reason, and a hold is placed only for a reason that is true on the date of the write.

## Hold reasons and what clears them

| Hold reason | When it may be recorded | What clears it, so the program resumes |
|---|---|---|
| Inpatient stay | The customer or caregiver reports a current inpatient admission to a hospital or skilled nursing facility, on tiers where an inpatient hold is required | Discharge reported |
| Coverage lapse | The coverage record the program bills has a termination date earlier than the date of the write and no other in-effect coverage on file fixes the program's tier | An in-effect coverage on file and written onto the program |
| Documentation lapse | No authorization grant of the program is valid on the date of the write | An authorization grant valid on the date of the write |
| Past-due balance | On tiers where the past-due age is greater than 0, the past-due amount is at least the tier's past-due hold amount and no approved payment plan covers it | A past-due amount below the past-due hold amount, or an approved payment plan |
| Customer request | The customer asks to pause shipments | The customer's own request |

A program on hold resumes only when its recorded hold reason has cleared. An inpatient admission is a fact the customer or caregiver reports, and a customer request is the customer's own; a coverage lapse, a documentation lapse and a past-due balance are read from Larkfield's records as they stand on the date of the write.

## The past-due amount

The past-due amount of a program on a test date is the greater of 0.00 and the following difference, in USD: the total of the remittance patient responsibility, patient charge and refund postings whose posting date is more than the tier's past-due age in calendar days before the test date, less the total of all payments and balance adjustments posted on or before the test date. Only patient-balance postings dated on or before the test date enter it, and payments and credits are applied to the oldest postings first.

*Hypothetical case:* with a past-due age of 90 days and a hold amount of 75.00, a program whose postings older than 90 days total 120.00 and whose payments and adjustments to date total 30.00 has a past-due amount of 90.00, which is at least 75.00; if payments and adjustments totalled 50.00 instead, the past-due amount would be 70.00, below the hold amount.

## Administrative closure

A program closes administratively, with the matching closure reason, in exactly these cases:

- **Documentation not received** — a program still in referral received or pending authorization once the date of the write is later than the enrolled date plus the tier's referral documentation window in calendar days, with no prior authorization decision pending;
- **Authorization denied** — a payer prior authorization denial stands and no new request is pending;
- **Hold limit reached** — a program on hold once the date of the write is later than the hold start date plus the tier's hold limit in calendar days;
- **Coverage ended** — a program on hold for coverage lapse whose customer reports no replacement coverage;
- **Customer discontinued** — the customer confirms the cancellation of a program on hold;
- **Deceased** — Larkfield's records team has recorded the customer's death.

Day counts in this policy are calendar days counted from the named date, and a closure is made only on a day strictly later than the named date plus the stated days.

| Hypothetical case (hold started 2026-01-10; hold limit 60 days) | Close for hold limit reached? |
|---|---|
| Date of the write 2026-03-11 (start date plus 60 days) | No — not strictly later |
| Date of the write 2026-03-12 | Yes |
